title: plan
description: A partitioned implementation plan — the contract between /taskplan (which writes it to docs/plan/<slug>.json) and /implement (which consumes it with zero re-planning). Every task carries checkable acceptance criteria, an explicit file boundary, a model tier, and a method; waves group file-disjoint tasks that run in parallel. If two tasks in one wave share a file, the partition is wrong — fix the plan, don't dispatch it.

slug.description: Kebab-case feature slug — reuse the spec's slug (docs/spec/<slug>.md -> docs/plan/<slug>.json).

spec.description: Path to the source spec (e.g. 'docs/spec/<slug>.md'), or empty string if the plan was built from a description.

createdWith.description: What produced this file, e.g. '/taskplan' — provenance for later analysis.

defaultMethod.description: The method every task inherits unless it overrides (per-task `method`). Each value is the instruction sentence /implement injects into the implementer brief's ## Method section.

tdd.description: The TDD rule, e.g. 'Write the failing test first (red), then the minimal code to pass (green), then refactor. Test files must sit inside this task's files_owned.'

sourceDriven.description: The source-grounding rule, e.g. 'Ground every API/library decision in official docs (context7/WebFetch); cite the source. Do not guess an API surface.'

incremental.description: The incremental-delivery rule, e.g. 'Ship the thinnest vertical slice that meets the criteria; gate risky/incomplete paths behind a feature flag with a safe default.'

tasks.description: The atomic, independent units of work (~100 lines of change each). A collapsed linear chain (A -> B -> C with nothing beside it) is ONE task with a multi-step brief.

id.description: Short unique task id, e.g. 'T1' — referenced by `depends_on` and `waves`.

title.description: One-line statement of the unit of work.

acceptance_criteria.description: Checkable contract — a test passes, an output matches. If you can't write crisp criteria, the task isn't understood yet.

files_owned.description: Exact globs/paths this task creates or modifies — the boundary that makes parallelism safe. Must include the task's own test files (or the tdd rule collides with the boundary). Disjoint from every other task in the same wave.

depends_on.description: Task ids this task needs finished first (e.g. it consumes their API). Empty array if independent. Dependencies land in earlier waves — don't fake parallelism.

model.description: Cheapest tier that clears the task's intelligence AND taste bar: haiku = mechanical/deterministic; sonnet = standard well-specified (the workhorse default); opus = subtle correctness or real design judgment. Fable is not available for delegation.

method.description: Optional per-task override of `defaultMethod` (e.g. a docs-only task relaxes tdd). Same keys; only the overridden ones need appear.

notes.description: Optional context for the implementer brief — pointers to existing code, the pattern to follow.

waves.description: Execution order: each wave is the list of task ids that run in parallel (their files_owned are pairwise disjoint; all their depends_on sit in earlier waves).

parallelWidth.description: W = size of the widest wave. W == 1 means the work is serial — /implement's width gate will reject it; route to a single implementer instead. Combined with volume V (task count after chain-collapse): W >= 2 and V >= 5 justify orchestration.
